description: issue #687 (slice I8): with the `interaction-events` profile active, a program that actually USES all five implemented Interaction forms — the `wait` primitive and the `when`/`every`/`on_key`/`on_click` block-heads — checks clean. The block-heads were already visible names (slices I3-I6); `wait` was NOT, so before I8 this program raised `ol-unknown-command` on line 2 even under an active profile — a profile whose own primitive is unknown is not conformant. I8 registers `interactionPrimitiveNames()` in `collectVisibleNames`' `interaction-events` gate, and this fixture is the proof the gap is closed. `wait` is placed inside a `[ ... ]` block inside `repeat` inside a procedure body so a fix that only handled a top-level occurrence cannot pass. This is a check-mode fixture: it proves static NAME VISIBILITY and arity only — it does not execute, so it asserts nothing about handler delivery (the `when`/`every`/`on_key`/`on_click` execution fixtures in the sibling directories cover that). The profile's `input` reporter is deliberately absent: its slice (#681, I2) is unimplemented, so registering it would be a false tooling claim.
